title: Coordinate Plane and Graphing
objectives: Plot points on the coordinate plane using ordered pairs
Graph linear equations and identify key features
Calculate and interpret slope as rate of change

introduction.context: GPS navigation, weather maps, and video game graphics all use coordinate systems to pinpoint locations. The coordinate plane is your mathematical GPS!
introduction.connection: Coordinate planes help us map locations, track trends in data, design computer graphics, and analyze relationships between variables in science and business.

concepts.title: Coordinate Plane
concepts.content: A two-dimensional grid formed by two perpendicular number lines called axes. The horizontal axis is called the x-axis, and the vertical axis is the y-axis. They intersect at the origin (0,0).
concepts.latex: \text{Point: } (x, y) \text{ where } x \text{ is horizontal, } y \text{ is vertical}

concepts.title: Slope
concepts.content: The steepness of a line, calculated as rise over run or change in y over change in x. Slope tells us how much y changes for each unit change in x.

examples.problem: Plot the point A(2, 3) on a coordinate plane
examples.solution: Point plotted at 2 right, 3 up from origin
commonErrors: Moving in wrong direction for negative coordinates

practice.problem: In which quadrant is the point (-3, 2)?
practice.explanation: Quadrant II has negative x-coordinates and positive y-coordinates.
hints: x is negative, y is positive

practice.problem: What is the slope of the line y = 3x - 4?
practice.explanation: In y = mx + b form, m is the slope. Here m = 3.
hints: Look at the coefficient of x
In y = mx + b, m is the slope
